questions.question: Based on the accepted values for the masses of the Earth and the Moon and the distance between them, what is the calculated gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the Moon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.02 x 10^20 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The gravitational force between the **Earth** and the **Moon** is calculated using **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**. This law states that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between their centers.
 
• The formula used for this calculation is **F = G (m1m2 / r²)**, where **F** is the gravitational force, **G** is the gravitational constant, **m1** and **m2** are the masses of the two bodies, and **r** is the distance between them.
 
• Based on accepted scientific data, the **mass of the Earth (m1)** is approximately **5.97 x 10^24 kg**, and the **mass of the Moon (m2)** is approximately **7.35 x 10^22 kg**.
 
• The average **distance (r)** between the centers of the Earth and the Moon is **3.84 x 10⁸ meters** (or 384,400 km).
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)** is a fixed value of **6.67 x 10^-11 N m²/kg²**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: **F = (6.67 x 10^-11) * [(5.97 x 10^24 * 7.35 x 10^22) / (3.84 x 10⁸)²]**, the resulting force is approximately **2.02 x 10^20 Newtons (N)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Gravitational Force**: Gravity is a **non-contact force** and is always **attractive** in nature. It acts along the line joining the centers of the two masses, making it a **central force**.
 
• **Orbital Stability**: This massive gravitational pull of **2.02 x 10^20 N** provides the **centripetal force** required to keep the Moon in its **elliptical orbit** around the Earth. Without this force, the Moon would move in a straight line into outer space due to its **inertia**.
 
• **Tidal Effects**: While the Earth exerts this force on the Moon, the Moon exerts an **equal and opposite force** on the Earth (consistent with **Newton's Third Law**). This lunar pull is the primary cause of **ocean tides** on Earth, creating tidal bulges in the hydrosphere.
 
• **Inverse Square Law**: The force of gravity follows the **inverse square law**. If the distance between the Earth and the Moon were to double, the gravitational force would drop to **one-fourth** of its current value (approximately **0.505 x 10^20 N**).
 
• **Comparison with Surface Gravity**: It is important not to confuse the gravitational force between two celestial bodies with the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**. On Earth's surface, **g** is **9.8 m/s²**, which represents the acceleration of an object, whereas the **2.02 x 10^20 N** is the total **magnitude of force** acting between the two planetary bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Henry Cavendish**: The value of the **Gravitational Constant (G)** was first experimentally determined by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798** using a torsion balance.
 
• **Barycenter**: The Earth and Moon actually orbit around their common **center of mass**, known as the **barycenter**. Because the Earth is so much more massive, the barycenter is located about **4,670 km** from the Earth's center, which is still **inside the Earth's interior** (about 1,700 km below the surface).
 
• **Unit of Force**: The **Newton (N)** is the SI unit of force, named after **Sir Isaac Newton**. One Newton is the force needed to accelerate **one kilogram** of mass at the rate of **one meter per second squared**.
 
• **Mass of the Moon**: The Moon's mass is about **1.2%** of the Earth's mass. This significant mass ratio (compared to other planet-satellite systems in our solar system) is why the gravitational interaction between the two is so powerful.
</ul

questions.question: One volt (1 V), the SI unit of potential difference, is defined when __________.

options.text: 1 joule of energy is dissipated in 1 second
1 coulomb of charge flows in 1 second
1 joule of work is done to move a charge of 1 coulomb
1 milliampere of current flows through 1 Ohm of resistance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 joule of work is done to move a charge of 1 coulomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potential Difference** between two points in an electric circuit is defined as the **amount of work done** in moving a **unit charge** from one point to the other.
 
• The **SI unit** of electric potential difference is the **Volt (V)**, named after the Italian physicist **Alessandro Volta**.
 
• One **Volt** is formally defined as the potential difference between two points in a current-carrying conductor when **1 Joule of work** is done to move a charge of **1 Coulomb** from one point to the other. ***Hence, the statement in option 3 is correct.***
 
• Mathematically, it is expressed as **V = W / Q**, where **V** is the potential difference, **W** is the work done in **Joules**, and **Q** is the quantity of charge in **Coulombs**.
 
• Option 1 mentions **1 joule of energy dissipated in 1 second**, which actually defines **1 Watt (W)**, the unit of **Power**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 2 mentions **1 coulomb of charge flowing in 1 second**, which defines **1 Ampere (A)**, the SI unit of **Electric Current**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Option 4 mentions **1 milliampere of current through 1 Ohm of resistance**; according to **Ohm's Law (V = I x R)**, this results in **0.001 Volts** or **1 millivolt (mV)**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Instrument for Measurement:** The potential difference is measured by an instrument called the **Voltmeter**. A voltmeter is always connected in **parallel** across the points between which the potential difference is to be measured.
 
• **Voltmeter Resistance:** To ensure that it does not significantly alter the current in the circuit, a voltmeter is designed to have very **high resistance**.
 
• **Ohm's Law Relationship:** The potential difference (V) across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current (I) flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. This is expressed as **V = I x R**, where **R** is the **Resistance**.
 
• **Electric Potential vs. Potential Difference:** While **Electric Potential** at a point is the work done to bring a unit positive charge from **infinity** to that point, **Potential Difference** specifically refers to the work done between two defined points in a circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Electric potential and potential difference are **scalar quantities**, meaning they have magnitude but no specific direction in space.
 
• **Standard Values:** In **India**, the standard domestic supply voltage is **220 V** with a frequency of **50 Hz**. Commercial batteries, such as **AA** or **AAA** alkaline cells, typically provide a potential difference of **1.5 V**.
 
• **Work and Energy:** Since **V = W / Q**, the work done (or energy transferred) can be calculated as **W = V x Q**. This relationship is fundamental in understanding electrical energy consumption.
 
• **High Voltage Transmission:** Long-distance power transmission is usually done at **high voltages** (e.g., **11 kV, 33 kV, or 400 kV**) to minimize energy loss due to heating in the transmission lines, as higher voltage allows for lower current for the same power level.
</ul

questions.question: Meenu starts from rest and pedals her bicycle to reach a speed of 5 m/s in 25 seconds. What is her acceleration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.2 m/s2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** with respect to **time**. Mathematically, it is expressed as **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, and **t** is the time taken.
 
• In the given problem, Meenu starts from **rest**, which means her **initial velocity (u)** is **0 m/s**.
 
• The **final velocity (v)** reached by Meenu is **5 m/s** after a duration of **25 seconds**.
 
• By substituting these values into the formula: **a = (5 m/s - 0 m/s) / 25 s**.
 
• The calculation results in **5 / 25**, which simplifies to **1/5** or **0.2 m/s2**. Thus, the acceleration of the bicycle is **0.2 m/s2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit of Acceleration:** The standard unit for measuring acceleration in the **International System of Units (SI)** is **meter per second squared (m/s2)**. It represents how many meters per second the velocity changes every second.
 
• **Vector Quantity:** Acceleration is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**. If an object slows down, the acceleration is in the opposite direction of the motion, often referred to as **deceleration** or **retardation**.
 
• **Equations of Motion:** This calculation is based on the **first equation of motion**, which is **v = u + at**. These equations, derived by **Sir Isaac Newton**, describe the relationship between velocity, acceleration, time, and displacement for objects moving with **uniform acceleration**.
 
• **Uniform vs. Non-uniform Acceleration:** If the velocity of an object changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, it is called **uniform acceleration**. If the rate of change of velocity is not constant, it is **non-uniform acceleration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Initial State:** Whenever a problem mentions that an object starts from **rest**, the **initial velocity (u)** must always be taken as **zero**.
 
• **Final State:** Conversely, if an object comes to a **halt** or **stops**, the **final velocity (v)** is considered **0 m/s**.
 
• **Graphical Representation:** On a **Velocity-Time graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration** of the object. A straight line indicates constant acceleration, while a curved line indicates changing acceleration.
 
• **Average Acceleration:** It is the total change in velocity divided by the total time interval. In this specific case, since the change is linear, the acceleration calculated is the **average acceleration** over the **25-second** period.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Newton’s Third Law?

options.text: A stone dropping freely toward the ground
A gun moving backward after firing a bullet
A rocket rising upward as gases are expelled downward
A horse pulling a loaded cart

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A stone dropping freely toward the ground**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion** states that for every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction. These forces always act on two different bodies.
 
• **A stone dropping freely toward the ground** is primarily an illustration of **Newton’s Second Law of Motion** and the **Universal Law of Gravitation**. The motion is defined by the force of gravity acting on a single mass, causing it to accelerate at **9.8 m/s²**. While a reaction force technically exists (the stone pulls the Earth), the scenario is the standard example for **F = ma**. ***Hence, statement 1 is not an example of the Third Law.***
 
• **A gun moving backward after firing a bullet** is a classic example of the **Third Law**. When the gun exerts a forward force on the bullet (**action**), the bullet exerts an equal and opposite backward force on the gun (**reaction**), known as **recoil**. ***Hence, statement 2 is an example of the Third Law.***
 
• **A rocket rising upward** functions on the principle of action and reaction. The rocket engine expels exhaust gases downward at very high velocity (**action**), and these gases exert an equal upward thrust on the rocket (**reaction**), allowing it to overcome Earth's gravity. ***Hence, statement 3 is an example of the Third Law.***
 
• **A horse pulling a loaded cart** involves the horse pushing the ground backward with its hooves (**action**), and the ground pushing the horse forward with an equal force (**reaction**). This interaction allows the horse to move the cart forward. ***Hence, statement 4 is an example of the Third Law.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion:**
 
 
• Also known as the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external **unbalanced force**.
 
• This law defines the concept of **inertia**, which is the inherent property of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**
 
 
• It states that the magnitude of the force is the product of **mass** and **acceleration** (**F = ma**).
 
• It provides a quantitative measure of force and relates it to the **rate of change of momentum**.
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum:**
 
 
• Closely linked to the **Third Law**, it states that the total momentum of an isolated system remains **constant** if no external forces act on it.
 
• This principle is used to calculate **recoil velocity** in firearms and propulsion in **jet engines**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• **Sir Isaac Newton** formulated these **three laws of motion** in his monumental work, **Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica**, first published in **1687**.
 
• These laws form the foundation of **Classical Mechanics**, which describes the motion of macroscopic objects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **action and reaction forces** mentioned in the **Third Law** never cancel each other out because they act on **different objects**, not the same one.
 
• **Universal Law of Gravitation:** Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between them.
 
• In the case of a falling stone, the **acceleration** of the Earth toward the stone is negligible due to the Earth's massive **mass** (approximately **5.97 × 10^24 kg**), which is why we only observe the stone moving.

4f

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly explains why carbon forms covalent bonds in organic compounds?

options.text: Carbon atoms have a full outer shell and do not react
Carbon has a high tendency to form positive ions
Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell and shares electrons to complete its octet
Carbon easily donates all its valence electrons to non-metals

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell and shares electrons to complete its octet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon** is a chemical element with the **atomic number 6** and the symbol **C**. It is a non-metal and belongs to **group 14** of the periodic table.
 
• The electronic configuration of carbon is **2, 4**. This means it has **four electrons** in its outermost shell (valence shell).
 
• According to the **Octet Rule**, atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to achieve a stable configuration of **eight electrons** in their valence shell, similar to noble gases.
 
• For carbon, gaining four electrons to form a **C4- anion** is difficult because a nucleus with only **6 protons** cannot easily hold onto **10 electrons**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Conversely, losing four electrons to form a **C4+ cation** requires an extremely large amount of **ionization energy** to overcome the electrostatic attraction of the nucleus. *Hence, statements 2 and 4 are incorrect.*
 
• To achieve stability, carbon resolves this by **sharing its four valence electrons** with other atoms (such as Hydrogen, Oxygen, or other Carbon atoms), resulting in the formation of **covalent bonds**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tetravalency of Carbon**:
 
 
• Since carbon has **four valence electrons**, it is capable of forming **four covalent bonds** with other atoms. This property is known as **tetravalency**.
 
• This allows carbon to form a vast variety of complex molecules, which is the basis of **Organic Chemistry**.
 
 
 
• **Catenation**:
 
 
• Carbon has the unique ability to form strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, giving rise to long chains and rings. This property is called **catenation**.
 
• The **C-C bond energy** is very high (approx **348 kJ/mol**), making these structures exceptionally stable.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Organic Compounds**:
 
 
• Most organic compounds are **poor conductors of electricity** because they do not have free electrons or ions to carry charge.
 
• They generally have **low melting and boiling points** compared to ionic compounds because the intermolecular forces (**Van der Waals forces**) are weaker than ionic bonds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Covalent Bond Types**:
 
 
• Carbon can form **single bonds** (sharing one pair of electrons), **double bonds** (sharing two pairs), or **triple bonds** (sharing three pairs).
 
• Example: In **Methane (CH4)**, carbon forms four single covalent bonds. In **Ethene (C2H4)**, it forms a double bond, and in **Ethyne (C2H2)**, it forms a triple bond.
 
 
 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**:
 
 
• Carbon exists in different physical forms called allotropes, such as **Diamond**, **Graphite**, and **Fullerenes**.
 
• In **Diamond**, each carbon atom is bonded to **four** others in a rigid **3D tetrahedral structure**, making it the hardest natural substance.
 
• In **Graphite**, each carbon atom is bonded to **three** others in **hexagonal layers**, leaving one free electron, which makes graphite a good **conductor of electricity**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: When fertilisation takes place inside the female body, it is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**internal fertilisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fertilisation** is the process of the fusion of a **male gamete (sperm)** with a **female gamete (ovum/egg)** to form a **zygote**.
 
• When this fusion occurs **inside the female body**, it is known as **internal fertilisation**. This process ensures that the **embryo** is protected from the external environment during its initial stages of development.
 
• Internal fertilisation is a characteristic feature of many **terrestrial animals**, including **mammals** (such as **humans**, **cows**, and **dogs**), **birds** (such as **hens**), and **reptiles**.
 
• In this method, the **male** deposits **sperm** into the **female reproductive tract**, where one sperm eventually fuses with the egg.
 
• This type of fertilisation has a **higher success rate** for the survival of the offspring compared to external fertilisation because the **zygote** develops in a controlled, **safe environment** within the mother's body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **External Fertilisation:**
 
 
• This process occurs when the fusion of **male and female gametes** takes place **outside the female body**, typically in an **aquatic medium** like **water**.
 
• It is common in **aquatic animals** such as **fish**, **starfish**, and **amphibians** like **frogs**.
 
• During the **breeding season** (often **spring** or **monsoon**), the female lays hundreds of **eggs** in the water, and the male releases **sperm** over them to facilitate fertilisation.
 
 
 
• **In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF):**
 
 
• **IVF** is a **medical technique** where fertilisation is carried out **outside the body** in a **laboratory** (often in a **glass** container or petri dish).
 
• It is primarily used for **couples** who face issues like **blocked oviducts**, which prevent natural internal fertilisation.
 
• The resulting **zygote** is allowed to develop for about **one week** in a controlled environment before being **implanted** into the mother's **uterus** for further growth.
 
 
 
• **Test-Tube Babies:**
 
 
• The term **"test-tube babies"** refers to infants born through the **IVF** technique.
 
• It is a **misnomer** because the baby does not actually grow in a test tube; only the **initial fertilisation** happens in a laboratory, while the rest of the **gestation** occurs in the mother's **womb**.
 
 
 
• **Zygote and Embryo:**
 
 
• The **zygote** is the **single cell** formed immediately after fertilisation.
 
• As the zygote **divides repeatedly**, it forms a ball of cells called an **embryo**, which then travels to the **uterus** to get embedded in the **uterine wall** for further development into a **foetus**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which hormone triggers sexual maturation in boys?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Testosterone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Testosterone** is the primary male sex hormone and an **androgen**, which plays a critical role in the **sexual maturation** of boys during **puberty**.
 
• It is primarily produced in the **testes** by the **Leydig cells**, under the influence of the **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** secreted by the **anterior pituitary gland**.
 
• This hormone triggers the development of **secondary sexual characteristics**, such as the growth of **facial, axillary, and pubic hair**, and the **deepening of the voice** due to the enlargement of the **larynx**.
 
• **Testosterone** is also responsible for the increase in **muscle mass**, **bone density**, and the stimulation of **spermatogenesis** (the production of sperm).
 
• While **Estrogen** and **Progesterone** are found in males in very small quantities, they are not the primary hormones for male maturation. ***Hence, the correct answer is Testosterone.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Estrogen:**
 
 
• It is the primary **female sex hormone** responsible for the development of female **secondary sexual characteristics**, such as **breast development** and the regulation of the **menstrual cycle**.
 
• In females, it is mainly produced in the **ovaries**.
 
 
 
• **Progesterone:**
 
 
• This hormone is primarily involved in the **female reproductive system**, playing a vital role in maintaining the **lining of the uterus (endometrium)** during **pregnancy**.
 
• It is secreted by the **corpus luteum** in the ovary after **ovulation** occurs.
 
 
 
• **Oxytocin:**
 
 
• Often referred to as the **"bonding hormone"** or **"love hormone,"** it is produced in the **hypothalamus** and released by the **posterior pituitary gland**.
 
• Its primary functions include stimulating **uterine contractions** during **childbirth** and the **let-down reflex** during **breastfeeding**.
 
 
 
• **Puberty in Boys:**
 
 
• The process of **sexual maturation** typically begins between the ages of **9 and 14 years**.
 
• The **Hypothalamus** releases **Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)**, which signals the **pituitary gland** to release **FSH (Follicle-Stimulating Hormone)** and **LH**, eventually leading to the production of **Testosterone**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Nature:** **Testosterone**, **Estrogen**, and **Progesterone** are all **steroid hormones** derived from **cholesterol**.
 
• **Anabolic Effects:** **Testosterone** has significant **anabolic effects**, meaning it promotes the synthesis of **proteins** and the growth of tissues with **androgen receptors**.
 
• **Regulatory Mechanism:** The production of sex hormones is regulated via a **negative feedback loop** involving the **Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Gonadal (HPG) axis**. When testosterone levels are high, the brain reduces the signals to produce more.
 
• **Secondary Characteristics:** Other male changes include **increased sebaceous gland activity** (often leading to **acne**) and a change in **body fat distribution** toward a more **android (apple-shaped)** pattern.
</ul

questions.question: A wire of a given material has length L and cross-sectional area A, with resistance R. If the wire is stretched to twice its length while keeping the volume constant, what will be its new resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4R**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **resistance (R)** of a uniform metallic conductor is directly proportional to its **length (L)** and inversely proportional to its **cross-sectional area (A)**. This is expressed by the formula **R = ρ (L/A)**, where **ρ (rho)** is the **electrical resistivity** of the material.
 
• When a wire is stretched, its **volume (V)** remains **constant**. The volume of a cylindrical wire is calculated as the product of its cross-sectional area and its length (**V = A × L**).
 
• If the wire is stretched to **twice its length**, the new length **L'** becomes **2L**. Because the **volume is constant**, the new area **A'** must decrease to maintain the equation **A × L = A' × (2L)**. This mathematical relationship implies that the new area **A' = A/2**. ***Hence, the change in area is a critical factor in determining the final resistance.***
 
• By substituting the new dimensions into the resistance formula, the new resistance **R'** becomes **ρ (2L / (A/2))**. This simplifies to **ρ (4L / A)**, which is **4 × R**. ***Hence, the new resistance is four times the original resistance.***
 
• This result demonstrates that stretching a wire increases resistance not just by increasing length, but also by making the wire thinner (reducing the area), both of which impede the flow of **electrons**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 4R.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Resistivity (ρ)**: This is an intrinsic property of a **material** that quantifies how strongly it opposes the flow of electric current. It does not depend on the dimensions (length or area) of the wire but depends on the **nature of the material** and the **temperature**. The **SI unit** of resistivity is the **Ohm-meter (Ω·m)**.
 
• **Ohm's Law**: Formulated by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the current passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant (**V = IR**).
 
• **Conductivity (σ)**: This is the inverse of resistivity (**σ = 1/ρ**). Materials with high **conductivity**, such as **silver** and **copper**, are excellent **conductors** of electricity and are commonly used in **electrical wiring**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance**:
 
 
• **Nature of Material**: Different materials have different densities of free **electrons**.

• **Types of Thyroid Hormones:** The gland produces two main hormones: **Triiodothyronine (T3)** and **Thyroxine (T4)**. Although **T4** is produced in larger quantities, **T3** is the more biologically active form.
 
• **Calcitonin:** Besides metabolic hormones, the thyroid also secretes **Calcitonin**, which helps in regulating **calcium levels** in the blood by promoting the deposition of calcium into the **bones**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the atomic number of an element?

options.text: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom
The number of electrons in the outermost shell of an atom
The number of neutrons in the nucleus of an atom
The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number** of an element is defined as the total number of **protons** present in the **nucleus** of an **atom**. It is traditionally represented by the symbol **'Z'**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The **atomic number** is a unique identifier for each chemical element. For instance, all **Hydrogen** atoms have an atomic number of **1**, while all **Carbon** atoms have an atomic number of **6**.
 
• In the **Modern Periodic Table**, elements are arranged in increasing order of their **atomic numbers**, as this property determines the **chemical identity** and characteristics of the element.
 
• Since an **atom** is electrically **neutral** in its ground state, the number of **protons** (positive charge) is exactly equal to the number of **electrons** (negative charge). However, the definition of the atomic number specifically refers to the **protons** because the number of electrons can change during **chemical reactions** or **ionization**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The number of **neutrons** in the **nucleus** can vary even among atoms of the same element. Atoms with the same **atomic number** but different numbers of **neutrons** are called **isotopes** (e.g., **Protium, Deuterium, and Tritium** for Hydrogen). *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Mass Number (A):**
 
 
• The **total number of protons and neutrons** in the **nucleus** is called the **mass number**, denoted by **'A'**. These subatomic particles are collectively known as **nucleons**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• The relationship between these values is given by the formula: **Mass Number (A) = Atomic Number (Z) + Number of Neutrons (N)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Periodic Law:** The **Modern Periodic Law** states that "the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their **atomic numbers**." This replaced **Mendeleev's** earlier concept based on **atomic mass**.
 
• **Representation:** In chemical notation, the **atomic number** is usually written as a **subscript** on the left side of the element's symbol, while the **mass number** is written as a **superscript**. For example, in **¹²₆C**, **6** is the atomic number and **12** is the mass number.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sound propagation is correct?

options.text: Sound travels faster in gases than in solids.
Sound travels in the form of transverse waves in air.
Sound requires a medium for propagation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sound requires a medium for propagation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound **is a **mechanical wave** that results from the back-and-forth **vibration** of the particles of the medium through which it moves. 
 
• **Statement 1** suggests that **sound **travels faster in **gases** than in **solids**. In reality, the speed of sound depends on the **density **and **elasticity **of the medium. Particles in **solids** are packed more tightly than in **liquids **or **gases**, allowing sound to travel fastest in **solids** (approximately **5000 m/s** in steel) and slowest in **gases** (about **343 m/s** in air). ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2** mentions that **sound **can travel in a **vacuum**. Since sound is a **mechanical wave**, it requires a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate. In a **vacuum**, such as **outer space**, there are no molecules to vibrate, meaning sound cannot travel. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3** states that **sound **travels as **transverse waves** in **air**. In fluids like air and water, sound travels as **longitudinal waves**, where the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction of energy transport. **Transverse waves** are those where particles move **perpendicular** to the wave direction, which is characteristic of **light **or waves on a string. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4** asserts that **sound requires a medium** for propagation. This is a fundamental property of mechanical waves. Sound energy is transferred through the **collisions **of atoms and molecules within a substance. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sound requires a medium for propagation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Sound Waves:**
 
 
• Sound waves are categorized as **longitudinal waves** because the displacement of the medium is in the same direction as the wave propagation.
 
• They consist of **compressions** (regions of high pressure and density) and **rarefactions** (regions of low pressure and density).
 
 
 
• **Speed of Sound Factors:**
 
 
• **Temperature:** The speed of sound increases with an increase in **temperature**. For every **1 degree Celsius** rise in temperature, the speed of sound in air increases by about **0.6 m/s**.
 
• **Humidity:** Sound travels faster in **humid air** than in dry air because moist air is less dense than dry air.
 
• **State of Matter:** Sound travels through **steel **about **15 times** faster than through **air**.
 
 
 
• **Human Audibility:**
 
 
• The **audible range** for the average human ear is between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• Sounds below **20 Hz** are termed **infrasonic**, while sounds above **20,000 Hz** are termed **ultrasonic**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bell Jar Experiment:** This is a classic experiment used to prove that **sound **needs a **medium**. As the air is removed from a **sealed jar** using a **vacuum pump**, the sound of an electric bell inside becomes fainter and eventually disappears, even though the hammer is still seen hitting the bell.
 
• **Reflection of Sound:** Like light, sound follows the **laws of reflection**. This phenomenon results in **echoes **and is used in technologies like **SONAR **(Sound Navigation and Ranging) and **ultrasound **imaging.
 
• **Characteristics of Sound:** Sound is defined by its **amplitude **(which determines **loudness**), **frequency **(which determines **pitch**), and **timbre **(the quality or **tone**).
</ul

questions.question: The defect of hypermetropia can be corrected by using which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convex lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypermetropia**, also known as **long-sightedness** or **farsightedness**, is a common vision defect where a person can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly.
 
• In a hypermetropic eye, the image of a nearby object is formed **behind the retina** instead of on it. This happens because the light rays do not converge enough by the time they reach the **retina**.
 
• This defect arises either because the **focal length** of the eye lens is too long or the **eyeball** has become too small.
 
• To correct this, a **convex lens** (converging lens) of appropriate **focal length** is used. The **convex lens** provides the additional **focusing power** needed to converge the light rays, ensuring the image is formed exactly on the **retina**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Convex lens.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Myopia (Near-sightedness):**
 
 
• In this defect, a person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects distinctly. The image is formed **in front of the retina**.
 
• It is corrected by using a **concave lens** (diverging lens), which diverges the incoming light rays so that the eye lens can focus them properly on the **retina**.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia:**
 
 
• This is a vision defect that usually occurs with **aging**. The power of accommodation of the eye decreases as the **ciliary muscles** weaken and the eye lens loses its flexibility.
 
• People suffering from this often require **bifocal lenses**, where the upper part is a **concave lens** (for distant vision) and the lower part is a **convex lens** (for near vision).
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism:**
 
 
• This defect occurs when the **cornea** is not spherical in shape, leading to light being focused at different points. It results in blurred vision for both near and far objects.
 
• It is corrected by using **cylindrical lenses**, which compensate for the uneven curvature of the **cornea** or lens.
 
 
 
• **Power of a Lens:**
 
 
• The **power (P)** of a lens is defined as the reciprocal of its **focal length (f)** in meters (**P = 1/f**).
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Dioptre (D)**. A **convex lens** has **positive power**, while a **concave lens** has **negative power**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **near point** for a normal human eye is approximately **25 cm**. For a hypermetropic eye, the **near point** is farther away than **25 cm**.
 
• The **far point** for a normal human eye is **infinity**. In myopic eyes, the **far point** is closer than **infinity**.
 
• The **retina** acts as a light-sensitive screen where the image is formed. It contains specialized cells called **rods and cones** that convert light into electrical signals sent to the brain via the **optic nerve**.
 
• The **Iris** controls the amount of light entering the eye by adjusting the size of the **pupil**.
 
• The human eye lens is a **fibrous, jelly-like material** that changes its shape to adjust **focal length**, a process known as **accommodation**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following shows movement but not locomotion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Movement** refers to the act of changing the position of one or more parts of the body relative to the whole organism, whereas **locomotion** is the movement of the entire organism from one place to another, resulting in a change of **location**.
 
• **Plants** are generally **stationary** or fixed in the **soil** by their roots; therefore, they do not exhibit **locomotion**. However, they show various types of **movements** such as the opening and closing of **flowers**, the bending of stems toward **light**, and the closing of leaves in response to **touch**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• A **Dog** is a multicellular animal that uses its **limbs** to move from one place to another for food, shelter, or protection. This represents both **movement** and **locomotion**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• A **Bird** utilizes **wings** for flying and **feet** for walking or perching, which allows it to change its **geographical position** entirely. This is a clear example of **locomotion**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• A **Human** uses **skeletal muscles** and **bones** to walk, run, jump, or swim. Since humans can move their whole body from point **A** to point **B**, they exhibit **locomotion**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Plant Movements:**
 
 
• **Tropic Movements (Tropisms):** These are **growth-dependent** movements in response to a stimulus. Examples include **Phototropism** (response to light), **Geotropism** (response to gravity), and **Hydrotropism** (response to water).
 
• **Nastic Movements:** These are **non-directional** movements that do not depend on growth. A classic example is **Thigmonasty**, seen in the **Mimosa pudica** (touch-me-not plant), where leaves fold inward when touched.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of Locomotion in Animals:**
 
 
• Locomotion is essential for **survival** in the animal kingdom. Animals move to find **nutrition**, seek a **mate**, escape from **predators**, or find suitable **climatic conditions**.
 
• In humans and many vertebrates, locomotion is achieved through the **musculoskeletal system**, coordinated by the **nervous system**.
 
 
 
• **Distinction between Movement and Locomotion:**
 
 
• All **locomotion** is **movement**, but all **movements** are not **locomotion**. For instance, the **beating of the heart** or **breathing** are movements occurring within the body, but they do not cause the organism to travel.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cellular Movement:** Even within stationary organisms like plants, **cytoplasmic streaming** (cyclosis) occurs, which is the **movement** of the fluid substance inside a living cell.
 
• **Evolutionary Context:** Plants evolved to be **autotrophs**, meaning they produce their own food via **photosynthesis** using **sunlight**. Since their "food" comes to them in the form of light and **minerals** from the soil, they do not need **locomotion**.
 
• **Anatomical Features:** Animals possess specialized **organs of locomotion** like **cilia**, **flagella**, **fins**, or **legs**, which are absent in higher plants.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following nutrients is a macronutrient?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potassium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Potassium (K)** is classified as a **macronutrient** because it is required by plants in relatively large amounts for their growth and development.
 
• **Macronutrients** are essential elements that are generally present in plant tissues in concentrations exceeding **10 mmole/kg** of dry matter.
 
• **Potassium** is absorbed by plants in the form of **potassium ions (K+)**. It is found in abundance within **meristematic tissues**, **buds**, **leaves**, and **root tips**. ***Hence, the correct option is Potassium.***
 
• The primary functions of **Potassium** include maintaining the **anion-cation balance** in cells, **protein synthesis**, the **opening and closing of stomata**, and the **activation of enzymes** involved in photosynthesis and respiration.
 
• Along with **Nitrogen (N)** and **Phosphorus (P)**, **Potassium** is considered a **Primary Macronutrient** often found in commercial fertilizers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Micronutrients**: These are elements required by plants in very small quantities, specifically less than **10 mmole/kg** of dry matter. These are also known as **trace elements**.
 
 
• **Copper (Cu)**: It is a **micronutrient** absorbed as **cupric ions (Cu2+)**. It is essential for the overall **metabolism** in plants and is associated with enzymes involved in **redox reactions**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Zinc (Zn)**: It is a **micronutrient** absorbed as **Zn2+ ions**. It is necessary for the **synthesis of auxin** (a plant hormone) and activates various enzymes like **carboxylases**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Iron (Fe)**: Although required in larger amounts than other micronutrients, it is still classified as a **micronutrient**. It is a key constituent of **ferredoxin** and **cytochromes** and is essential for the formation of **chlorophyll**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• There are **17 essential elements** required for plant growth, which are categorized based on their quantitative requirements.
 
• **The 9 Macronutrients** include: **Carbon (C)**, **Hydrogen (H)**, **Oxygen (O)**, **Nitrogen (N)**, **Phosphorus (P)**, **Potassium (K)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, and **Sulphur (S)**.
 
• **The 8 Micronutrients** include: **Iron (Fe)**, **Manganese (Mn)**, **Copper (Cu)**, **Molybdenum (Mo)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Boron (B)**, **Chlorine (Cl)**, and **Nickel (Ni)**.
 
• **Carbon, Hydrogen, and Oxygen** are mainly obtained from **CO2** and **H2O**, while the others are absorbed from the soil as mineral nutrients.
 
• **Deficiency** of these nutrients can lead to various physiological disorders such as **Chlorosis** (yellowing of leaves), **Necrosis** (death of tissues), and **stunted growth**.
</ul

questions.question: Which statement is INCORRECT about contraceptive pills?

options.text: They can cause side effects like irregular bleeding or nausea in some users.
They contain synthetic hormones (estrogen and progesterone) that prevent ovulation,
They are a highly effective form of birth control when taken correctly.
They protect against sexually transmitted infections.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They protect against sexually transmitted infections.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Contraceptive pills**, often referred to as oral contraceptive pills (OCPs), primarily function by using **synthetic hormones** such as **estrogen** and **progesterone** to suppress the release of eggs from the ovaries, a process known as **ovulation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• These pills are considered a **highly effective** method of birth control; when taken consistently at the **same time every day**, they have a **perfect-use efficacy rate** of over **99%**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• While generally safe, hormonal contraceptives can cause **side effects** in some users, including **nausea**, **breast tenderness**, **headaches**, and **irregular bleeding** or spotting between periods. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It is a common medical fact that oral contraceptive pills **do not provide any protection** against **Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)** or **HIV/AIDS**, as they do not act as a physical barrier to prevent the exchange of bodily fluids. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Because they do not prevent **STIs**, health organizations often recommend "dual protection," which involves using both the **pill** for pregnancy prevention and **condoms** to reduce infection risks. ***Hence, the incorrect statement is 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanism of Action:**
 
 
• Beyond inhibiting **ovulation**, hormonal pills work by thickening the **cervical mucus**, which makes it difficult for **sperm** to enter the **uterus** and reach an egg.
 
• They also thin the lining of the **uterus** (the **endometrium**), making it less likely for a fertilized egg to implant itself.
 
 
 
• **Types of Pills:**
 
 
• **Combined Oral Contraceptives (COCs):** These contain both **estrogen** and **progestin**. They are the most common type and come in various **dosage** formats.
 
• **Progestogen-only pills (POPs):** Also known as the **mini-pill**, these do not contain **estrogen** and are often prescribed for women who are **breastfeeding** or have specific **health risks** like high blood pressure.
 
 
 
• **Non-Contraceptive Benefits:**
 
 
• Medical practitioners often prescribe these pills to manage conditions like **Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)**, **endometriosis**, and severe **menstrual cramps**.
 
• Long-term use of the **pill** has also been associated with a **reduced risk** of **ovarian** and **endometrial cancers**.

• In this specific case, the **constant force (F)** is given as **20 N** and the **displacement (d)** is **5 m**.
 
• Since the object moves in the **same direction** as the force, the **angle (θ)** is **0 degrees**. The value of **cos(0°)** is **1**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **W = 20 N × 5 m × 1 = 100 J**. Thus, the work done is **100 Joules**.

questions.question:
Select the correct option regarding the following two statements labelled Assertion (A) and Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a substance loses oxygen during a reaction, it is said to be reduced.
Reason (R): Reduction is defined as the gain of hydrogen or loss of oxygen.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that if a substance loses **oxygen** during a chemical reaction, it is said to be **reduced**. In classical chemistry, the removal of oxygen from a compound is one of the primary identifiers of a **reduction reaction**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** provides the definition of **reduction**, stating it is the **gain of hydrogen** or the **loss of oxygen**. This is the fundamental classical definition used to identify reduction in **redox reactions**. ***Hence, statement R is correct.***
 
• In the context of the given statements, the **Assertion** describes a specific scenario (loss of oxygen), and the **Reason** provides the general rule or definition that encompasses that scenario.
 
• Because the definition in **Reason (R)** directly confirms why the process mentioned in **Assertion (A)** is classified as reduction, it serves as the **correct explanation** for the assertion.
 
• An example of this is the reaction between **Copper Oxide (CuO)** and **Hydrogen (H2)**, where **CuO** loses oxygen to become **metallic Copper (Cu)**; here, the copper oxide is **reduced**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxidation:** This is the chemical process that acts as the opposite of reduction. It is defined as the **gain of oxygen** or the **loss of hydrogen** by a substance. In a reaction like **2Mg + O2 → 2MgO**, **Magnesium** undergoes **oxidation** as it gains oxygen.
 
• **Redox Reactions:** The term **Redox** is a portmanteau of **Reduction** and **Oxidation**. In most chemical reactions involving these processes, they occur **simultaneously**. If one substance is reduced (loses oxygen), another must be oxidized (gains that oxygen).
 
• **Reducing and Oxidizing Agents:**
 
 
• A **Reducing Agent** is a substance that facilitates reduction by losing **hydrogen** or gaining **oxygen** (it gets oxidized itself).
 
• An **Oxidizing Agent** is a substance that facilitates oxidation by providing **oxygen** or accepting **hydrogen** (it gets reduced itself).
 
 
 
• **Modern Electronic Concept:** While the classical definition focuses on **oxygen** and **hydrogen**, the modern definition focuses on **electrons**. **Oxidation** is the **loss of electrons** (**OIL**: Oxidation Is Loss), while **Reduction** is the **gain of electrons** (**RIG**: Reduction Is Gain).
 
• **Practical Examples:** The **corrosion** of metals (like **rusting of iron**) and **rancidity** of fats/oils are common everyday examples of **oxidation** processes. In **rusting**, iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of moisture to form **Hydrated Iron (III) Oxide**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Oxidation State:** During **reduction**, the **oxidation state** (or oxidation number) of an element **decreases** (becomes more negative or less positive). During **oxidation**, the **oxidation state increases**.
 
• **Electronegativity:** In a broader sense, **oxidation** is the addition of an **electronegative element**, and **reduction** is the addition of an **electropositive element**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The term **reduction** originally comes from the **metallurgical** process of "reducing" a metal ore (like **Iron Oxide**) to its pure **metallic form** by removing oxygen, which results in a "reduction" in the mass of the ore.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct?

options.text: Shorter wavelengths scatter more than longer wavelengths.
The sky appears blue because air absorbs blue light.
The Tyndall effect can be used to detect colloids.
Scattering depends on the wavelength of light.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The sky appears blue because air absorbs blue light.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rayleigh Scattering** states that the amount of scattering is inversely proportional to the **fourth power** of the **wavelength** of light. This means that **shorter wavelengths** (such as blue and violet) are scattered much more efficiently than **longer wavelengths** (such as red). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The blue appearance of the sky is a result of **scattering**, not absorption. When sunlight enters the **Earth's atmosphere**, it strikes gas molecules and scatters in all directions. Because blue light has a **shorter wavelength**, it is scattered more widely than other colors, making the sky look blue to our eyes. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Tyndall effect** is the process of light scattering by **colloidal particles** or particles in a very fine suspension. It is a reliable method used in laboratories to **detect colloids** and distinguish them from true solutions, where the particles are too small to scatter light. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Scattering is fundamentally dependent on the **wavelength** of the incident light. The interaction between light and atmospheric particles (like **Nitrogen** and **Oxygen** molecules) changes based on the light's color and frequency. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is "The sky appears blue because air absorbs blue light" as it is the only incorrect statement.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Visible Spectrum:** The human eye can perceive light within the **visible spectrum**, which ranges from approximately **400 nm** (violet) to **700 nm** (red). **Blue light** typically has a wavelength between **450 and 495 nm**, while **red light** ranges from **620 to 750 nm**.
 
• **Mechanism of Tyndall Effect:** In a **colloid**, the particle size ranges between **1 nanometer** and **1000 nanometers**. These particles are large enough to deflect light rays, making the path of a beam (like a **laser** or **flashlight**) visible when passed through the mixture.
 
• **Atmospheric Phenomena:** At **sunrise** and **sunset**, sunlight must travel through a much thicker layer of the **atmosphere**. During this long journey, most of the **shorter wavelength** blue light is scattered away, leaving only the **longer wavelength** red and orange light to reach our eyes.
 
• **Lord Rayleigh's Contribution:** The **Rayleigh Scattering Law** was formulated in the **19th century**. It explains why the sky is blue and why the sun appears yellow/red. It specifically applies when the scattering particles are much smaller than the wavelength of the light, such as **individual molecules**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Color of the Sun:** Outside the atmosphere, the Sun appears **white** because all wavelengths reach the eye without being scattered. The **yellowish** hue we see from Earth is due to the removal of blue light from the direct beam by the atmosphere.
 
• **Effect of Particle Size:** If the Earth had no atmosphere, the sky would appear **completely black**, as seen by **astronauts** in space. Larger particles like **dust** and **water droplets** (in clouds) scatter all wavelengths of light almost equally, which is why **clouds appear white** (Mie scattering).
 
• **Violet vs. Blue:** Although **violet light** has an even shorter wavelength than blue light and scatters more, the sky appears blue because the **Sun emits more blue light** than violet, and the **human eye** is more sensitive to blue.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following metals reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zinc (Zn)** is a moderately reactive metal that reacts readily with **dilute Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** to produce **Zinc Chloride (ZnCl₂)** and evolve **Hydrogen gas (H₂)**.
 
• This reaction is a classic example of a **single displacement reaction**, where a more reactive metal displaces hydrogen from an acid. The chemical equation for this process is: **Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**. ***Hence, the option Zinc is correct.***
 
• In the **reactivity series** of metals, **Zinc** is positioned above **Hydrogen**. This higher position indicates that it has a greater tendency to lose electrons and undergo **oxidation** compared to hydrogen.
 
• During the reaction, **Zinc atoms** lose two electrons to form **Zn²⁺ ions** (oxidation), while **Hydrogen ions (H⁺)** from the acid gain these electrons to form **Hydrogen gas** (reduction).
 
• In contrast, metals like **Copper**, **Silver**, and **Gold** are placed below hydrogen in the **reactivity series**. Because they are less reactive than hydrogen, they cannot displace it from dilute acids. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series:** 
 
 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in descending order of their chemical reactivity. Metals at the top, such as **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)**, are highly reactive and can react even with cold water.
 
• Metals located **above Hydrogen** in the series (like **Magnesium**, **Aluminum**, **Zinc**, and **Iron**) can displace hydrogen from dilute acids like **HCl** or **H₂SO₄**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Hydrogen Gas:**
 
 
• The **Hydrogen gas** produced during the reaction is colorless and odorless. It can be identified using the **"Pop" test**: when a burning splinter is brought near the mouth of the test tube containing the gas, it burns with a characteristic **pop sound**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Noble Metals:**
 
 
• **Gold (Au)** and **Silver (Ag)** are known as **noble metals** because they are chemically inert and do not react with ordinary dilute acids. **Gold** only dissolves in a special mixture called **Aqua Regia** (a **3:1** mixture of concentrated **HCl** and **HNO₃**).
 
• **Copper (Cu)** is also relatively unreactive and does not produce hydrogen with dilute **HCl**, although it may react with oxidizing acids like concentrated **Nitric acid**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Zinc Metal:** It has the **atomic number 30** and is commonly used in **galvanization** to prevent the rusting of iron. In the laboratory, **granulated zinc** is preferred for producing hydrogen gas because its larger surface area increases the **rate of reaction**.
 
• **Acid Strength:** While **Zinc** reacts with dilute **HCl** and **H₂SO₄** to give hydrogen, it does not typically produce hydrogen gas with **Nitric acid (HNO₃)**. This is because **HNO₃** is a **strong oxidizing agent** that oxidizes the produced hydrogen into **water (H₂O)** and itself gets reduced to nitrogen oxides.
 
• **Displacement Logic:** The ability of a metal to react with an acid depends on its **electrode potential**. Metals with a **negative reduction potential** (relative to the standard hydrogen electrode) are capable of liberating hydrogen gas from acids.

questions.question: Which of the following plant tissues is made up of cells that are dead at maturity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sclerenchyma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sclerenchyma** is a simple permanent plant tissue characterized by cells that are **dead at maturity**. These cells lose their **protoplasm** during development, leaving behind only the cell wall. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The cell walls of **sclerenchyma** are significantly thickened due to the deposition of **lignin**, a complex polymer that acts as a waterproof cementing material.
 
• Due to the extreme thickness of the **lignified** walls, there are no **intercellular spaces** between the cells, making the tissue very dense and rigid.
 
• The primary **function** of **sclerenchyma** is to provide **mechanical strength** and structural rigidity to the plant, allowing it to withstand environmental stresses like wind and weight.
 
• This tissue is commonly found in the **stems** (around vascular bundles), in the **veins of leaves**, and in the **hard coverings** of seeds and nuts, such as the shell of a **coconut**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma**:
 
 
• This is the most fundamental and abundant simple tissue in plants. The cells are **living** with thin cell walls made of **cellulose**.
 
• They possess large **central vacuoles** and are involved in **photosynthesis**, **storage** of food, and **secretion**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma**:
 
 
• This tissue consists of **living cells** that are elongated and have **unevenly thickened** cell walls, particularly at the corners.
 
• The thickening is due to the deposition of **cellulose**, **hemicellulose**, and **pectin**. It provides **flexibility** and mechanical support to young growing parts like the **petiole** of a leaf. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Aerenchyma**:
 
 
• It is a specialized type of **parenchyma** found in **hydrophytes** (aquatic plants).
 
• It contains large **air cavities** or spaces that facilitate the exchange of gases and provide **buoyancy** to the plant, helping it float. Since it is a parenchyma variant, its cells are **living**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Sclerenchyma**:
 
 
• **Fibers**: These are long, narrow, and thick-walled cells with **tapering ends**. They usually occur in bundles and are used commercially in making **ropes** and **textiles** (e.g., **jute** and **hemp**).
 
• **Sclereids**: Also known as **stone cells**, these are spherical or oval cells with extremely thick walls and very narrow **lumens**. They are responsible for the **gritty texture** found in fruits like **pears** and **sapota**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Composition**:
 
 
• The presence of **lignin** is a key distinguishing **feature** of sclerenchyma compared to collenchyma (which uses pectin) and parenchyma (which uses thin cellulose). **Lignification** is the process that eventually leads to the death of the **protoplast**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison**:
 
 
• While **Xylem** (a complex tissue) also contains dead cells like **tracheids** and **vessels** for water transport, **sclerenchyma** is the primary **simple permanent tissue** dedicated solely to **mechanical protection**.
 
 
</ul
